answer: A stake-and-slash bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks collateral that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spawning a thousand mirror copies costs a thousand bonds. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a comet gathering a tail over many verified epochs, and cannot be bought or transferred, so no ivory-tower shortcut exists. An attacker must pay real capital per identity and wait through the same slow history as everyone else, which turns a cheap Sybil flood into a costly, slow grind.
